In brief: leadership is wrong. The 45-minute pipeline consumes only ~19% of a workday, so duration alone isn't the throughput bottleneck — the binding constraint is that only one deploy can be "in flight" at a time (the single coordinated restart plus the human cadence norms around it). Microservices wouldn't fix that for this team: checkout/inventory/fulfillment are stipulated as transactionally coupled, so cross-cutting deploys (most of what this domain needs) get no faster and likely slower under decomposition, while a 12-engineer team sits below the size where service/team alignment (Conway's Law) pays off. A cost estimate puts monolith CI/process optimization (test sharding, trunk-based dev + flags, rolling restarts) at ~2–4 engineer-months versus ~10–42+ for full decomposition, for a comparable or better outcome. Recommendation: do the CI/process fix now, modularize internally in parallel, and defer any service extraction until a specific loosely-coupled edge (e.g., search) proves it's needed. Overall confidence: MEDIUM, capped by named, priced assumptions (queueing-model fit and the coupling claim) rather than by any unresolved rival.
